newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian blue chips lead slow market recovery.
newsitem.headline: Croatian blue chips lead slow market recovery.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed the week mixed on Friday, with blue chips recovering from recent losses and analysts expected them to give the market a much needed boost in the days ahead.
"I see mild growth for liquid stocks from the beginning of next week," said Davor Relja, analyst at the Faktor brokerage.
"As (fully-listed) Zagrebacka Banka and (drugs firm) Pliva are now on the rise again, other stocks will follow in their footsteps."
These two regularly dictate the market mood. But more active foreign buying has recently also propped up the prices of other liquid stocks up.
Trading livened up on Friday, boosting volume to 22,530 from 9,503 units. Turnover tripled to 18.3 million kuna. Five of 11 active stocks five rose, four fell and two were flat.
Investors seemed to have got over their nervousness about trading limitations imposed in neighbouring Slovenia, market watchers said.

After scarce interest earlier in the week, Zagrebacka and Pliva both traded on higher volumes, rebounding to close firmer in line with the recovery of their global depositary receipts (GDRs) in London.
Zagrebacka, selling 6,422 shares, ended 70 kuna or 3.89 percent higher at 1,870 kuna. Its 1/10 GDRs rose to $31.88 from $30.87 at the open on Seaq International.
Pliva added 13 kuna or 2.74 percent to 488 kuna on volume of 4,146 units. Its GDRs traded around $16.87 in London, up from $16.75 on Thursday.
Top gainer was chocolate maker Kras, rising 25 kuna or 5.55 percent to 475 kuna on volume of 866 shares.
Another hotel stock Istraturist was the biggest decliner, losing 38 kuna or 16.67 percent to 190 on volume of 824 shares.
Among hoteliers Arenaturist and Jadranturist were the only steady gainers, inching up 10 and two kuna respectively to 190 and 330 with 109 and 420 units sold.
Most active food processor Podravka held its ground at 320 kuna, selling 8,668 shares.
